Rashi on Nazir 43a:11:1.english: They objected: A person - This is the beginning of the baraita in [the chapter entitled] HaOhr VeHaRotev.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:11:2.hebrew: מגוייד - חתוך לאיבריו, ואפילו הכי אינו מטמא. וקשיא לר"ל, דמשמע ליה מלהחלו דאפילו לגוסס אסור:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:11:2.english: Severely lacerated - Cut at his limbs; and even so, he does not impart ritual impurity. And [this is] difficult for Reish Lakish, for whom [the verse] “to profane himself” indicates that [contracting impurity from] even a dying person is forbidden.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:11:3.hebrew: לא קשיא לענין טמויי - הוא דלא מטמא עד שתצא נפשו, ולא כשהוא גוסס; אבל לענין אחולי — מכיון דהוי גוסס, קאי בלאו ד״לא יחלל״:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:11:3.english: [This is] not difficult: With regard to imparting impurity - It is [only] that he does not impart impurity until his soul departs, and not when he is dying; but with regard to profaning — once he is dying, he is subject to the negative prohibition of: “He shall not profane [the sanctuary of his God]” (Leviticus 21:12).

Rashi on Nazir 43a:1:1.hebrew: בבית - אמאי חייב שתים? הא לא אתיין בהדדי! דכיון דעייל ידיה, דאורחיה דאיניש בהכי, איטמי ליה, דכמאן דנגע בטומאת המת שבפנים דמי; וביאה לא הוי עד דעייל כוליה גופיה:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:1:1.english: In a house - Why is he liable [for] two [sets of lashes]? Surely they do not occur simultaneously! For once he inserts his hands — as that is the normal way of a person — he has become ritually impure, as he is considered like one who touched the corpse impurity that is inside; whereas "entering" does not occur until his entire body enters.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:1.hebrew: אלא אמר ר"א צירף ידו - כל היכא דהושיט ידו ליכנס תחלה:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:1.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said: He joined his hand - Whenever he extended his hand to enter first.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:2.hebrew: משום טומאה איכא משום ביאה ליכא - ולא הוי כמאן דאתיין טומאה וביאה בהדי הדדי, ואינו חייב אלא אחת, שהרי כבר מחולל ועומד הוא. אלא הכא במאי עסקינן? דצירף גופו — כלומר, שהכניס כל גופו כאחד — דטומאה וביאה בהדי הדדי קאתיין:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:2.english: There is [liability] due to defilement, there is no [liability] due to entry - And [so] it is not considered as [a case where] defilement and entry come simultaneously, and he is liable for only one [count], since he is already desecrated. Rather, what are we dealing with here? Where he joined his body — that is to say, that he brought in his entire body at once — so that defilement and entry come simultaneously.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:3.hebrew: צירף גופו - לאו דוקא, אלא איידי דאמר צירף ידו, קאמר צירף גופו:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:3.english: He joined his body - [This phrasing] is not precise; rather, since it said "he joined his hand," it said "he joined his body."

Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:4.hebrew: והא לא אפשר דלא עייל חוטמו ברישא - משום דבולט מן הפרצוף, דאורחיה דאינש לכי עייל בביתיה דשוחה ראשו ברישא, ונחית ליה טומאה. ולא הויא [ביאה] עד דעייל ליה כוליה, וכי עייל כוליה גופיה — הא מיטמי וקאי:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:2:4.english: But is it not impossible that his nose would not enter first - Because it protrudes from the face, as it is a person's way when entering a house to bow his head first, and [ritual] impurity descends upon him. And it is not [considered] entry until all of him enters it; and when his entire body enters, he is already impure.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:3:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא הכניס ידו כו' - אלא היכי משכחת לה? כגון דהכניס גופו, שנכנס כשהוא זקוף, דאתיין להו טומאה וביאה בהדדי, וחייב שתים:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:3:1.english: Rather, Rava said: [If] he brought in his hand, etc. - Rather, how do you find [such a case]? For example, where he brought in his body, [meaning] that he entered while upright, so that impurity and entry come together, and he is liable on two [counts].

Rashi on Nazir 43a:3:2.english: And still, it is impossible that the toes of his feet would not enter - etc.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:4:1.hebrew: כגון שנכנס - לבית שבתוכה טומאת מת, בשידה תיבה ומגדל':
Rashi on Nazir 43a:4:1.english: Where one entered - Into a house within which is the impurity of a corpse, in a chest, a box, or a cabinet.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:5:1.hebrew: ת"ר לא יטמא בעל בעמיו להחלו עד שעה שימות - מותר לעסוק בו, ואינו עובר עליו משום לא יחלל עד שעה שימות. והאי קרא קאי בכהן, והוא הדין לנזיר:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:5:1.english: The Sages taught: “He shall not become impure, a chief among his people, to profane himself,” until the time that he dies - It is permitted to attend to him, and he does not violate [a prohibition] regarding him on account of [the prohibition] “he shall not profane” until the time that he dies. And this verse refers to a priest, and the same law applies to a nazirite.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:5:2.hebrew: רבי אומר לא יטמא להם במותם עד שימות - והאי קרא בנזיר קאי, והוא הדין בכהן:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:5:2.english: Rabbi says: “He shall not become impure for them when they die,” until he dies - And this verse refers to a nazirite, and the same law applies to a priest.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:6:1.hebrew: משמעות דורשין - דלמר משמע ליה מהאי קרא, דעד שעה שימות, אע"ג דעסיק ביה — לא הוי מחולל; ולמר — מהאי קרא דלהחלו:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:6:1.english: The interpretation of the meaning - For to one Master, it is understood from this verse that until the time that he dies, even though he attends to him, he does not become profaned; and to [the other] Master, [it is understood] from this verse: “to profane himself.”

Rashi on Nazir 43a:6:2.hebrew: ור"ל אמר גוסס איכא בינייהו - דלמאן דמשמע ליה מלהחלו, אפילו בגוסס קאי בלא יחלל, דכיון שהוא גוסס סופו להיות חלל, דקי"ל (גיטין דף כח.) רוב גוססין למיתה, וקאמר דלא יחלל כו'. ולמאן דמשמע ליה מבמותם, עד שימות אינו עובר בלא יטמא, לא כהן ולא נזיר; אבל בגוסס — לית לן בה:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:6:2.english: And Reish Lakish said: [The difference] between them is a dying person - For according to the one for whom [the prohibition] is inferred from "to profane himself," even with regard to a dying person [a priest] is subject to [the prohibition of] "he shall not profane [himself]," for since he is dying, he is ultimately destined to become a corpse, as we maintain (Gittin 28a) that most dying people [proceed] to death, and [the verse] states that he shall not profane [himself], etc. And according to the one for whom it is inferred from "at their death," until he dies he does not violate "he shall not defile himself" — neither a priest nor a nazirite; but with a dying person, we have no [prohibition] regarding it.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:7:1.hebrew: אבל מיטמא - בין נזיר בין כהן בנגעם ובזיבתם, ואינם עוברים במגע הזב — לא משום ״לא יחלל״ ולא משום ״לא יטמא״:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:7:1.english: However, he may become impure - Both a nazirite and a priest [may become impure] through their [relatives'] afflictions and through their discharge; and they do not transgress through contact with a zav — neither on account of “he shall not profane” nor on account of “he shall not defile himself.”

Rashi on Nazir 43a:8:1.hebrew: הא מיבעי ליה להאי סברא - במותם אין מטמאין, אבל מטמאין בנגעם ובזיבתם:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:8:1.english: Doesn’t he require it for this reasoning - [Namely:] Upon their death they may not become impure, but they may become impure from their [leprous] affliction and from their discharge.

Rashi on Nazir 43a:8:2.hebrew: א"כ - דלא נדרוש ליה אלא חד טעמא, נימא קרא "להחל", דמשמע לענין מי שאינו מחולל; ומדקאמר "להחלו", שמע מינה תרתי:
Rashi on Nazir 43a:8:2.english: If so - That [if] we were not to expound from it more than one rationale, let the verse state: “To profane,” which implies regarding one who is not [already] profaned; and from [the fact] that it says “to profane himself,” learn from it two [rulings].

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:10:1.hebrew: אם כן נימא קרא להחל מאי להחלו מיתיבי האדם אינו מטמא עד שתצא נפשו ואפילו מגוייד - פירוש: לשון "גודו אילנא" (דניאל ד), מלא פצעים [ופגמים]. והתם בפ' האשה (יבמות דף קכ:) [דייק] מהך ברייתא דמגוייד לא חיי: טמויי לא מטמא, הא מחייא לא; ופליגי ביה תנאי התם:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:10:1.english: "If so, let the verse state: 'To profane'; what is 'To profane himself'? They raised an objection: A person does not impart impurity until his soul departs, and even if he has severe lacerations" - Explanation: [This is an] expression [similar to] "Chop down [godu] the tree" (Daniel 4), [meaning] full of wounds [and gashes]. And there in the chapter [entitled] Ha'ishah (Yevamot 120b), [the Gemara infers] from this baraita that a severely lacerated person will not live: [It is only regarding] imparting impurity that he does not impart impurity, but [as for] living, he will not live; and tanna'im dispute it there.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:11:1.hebrew: ולמ"ד מלהחלו הא קתני: ואינו מטמא עד שימות - מכל מקום, נדרש לאו ד"לא יטמא" כאילו סמכו "להחלו", להזהירו אף על גוסס משום חילול; והוי מצי לשנויי דהך ברייתא כו':
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:11:1.english: “And according to the one who says [it is derived] from ‘to profane himself,’ doesn't it teach: ‘And he does not impart impurity until he dies’?” - Nevertheless, the negative commandment of “he shall not defile himself” is expounded as though [Scripture] juxtaposed “to profane himself” [to it], to caution him [the priest] even regarding a dying person on account of profanation. And [the Gemara] could have answered that this baraita [follows Rabbi, who holds that a dying person is not included, but it preferred to reconcile it with both views].

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:11:2.hebrew: ומהכא שמעינן דכהן אינו מוזהר על הגוסס, <abbr title="דקיימא לן">דקי"ל</abbr> כר' יוחנן לגבי <abbr title="ריש לקיש">ר"ל</abbr>. ומיהו <abbr title="בהלכות גדולות">בה"ג</abbr> גריס אביי במקום רבי יוחנן ורבא במקום <abbr title="ריש לקיש">ר"ל</abbr>, <abbr title="ולפי זה">ולפ"ז</abbr> הלכה כרבא לגבי דאביי. [ולרבא] פליגי רבי ורבנן, ואית לן הלכה כרבי מחבירו [ולא מחביריו, נמצא] יהא כהן מוזהר על גוסס:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:11:2.english: And from here we learn that a priest is not cautioned regarding a dying person [goses], for we hold in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan over Reish Lakish. However, the Halakhot Gedolot has the reading of Abaye in place of Rabbi Yoḥanan and Rava in place of Reish Lakish, and according to this, the halakha is in accordance with Rava over Abaye. [And according to Rava,] Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] and the Rabbis disagree, and we have [a principle that] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi [when he differs] from his colleague [but not from his colleagues; it thus follows that] a priest should be cautioned regarding a dying person.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:1:1.hebrew: בבית נמי כיון דאעיל ידיה אסתאב - דאהל המת כמליא טומאה דמי, ומיד שהושיט ידו מבפנים — כאילו נגע במת, ואכתי לא קרינן "לא יבא". וכי עייל כולי, האי טמא ומחולל ועומד הוא! ואתרי לא תמצא חיוב "לא יבא" עם "לא יטמא" — [כיון] שהוא מחולל ועומד, לא היה לנו לרבות "להחלו" למעט מחולל ועומד הוא, אלא לדרשה אחריתי כדבסמוך:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:1:1.english: "Into a house too, once he inserts his hand he becomes impure" - For a tent [containing] a corpse is considered as if full of ritual impurity, and immediately upon extending his hand inside, [it is] as though he touched the corpse, and yet we do not yet apply [to him the prohibition of] "he shall not enter." And when all of him enters, this person is [already] impure and standing in his profaned state! And on two [counts] you would not find liability for "he shall not enter" together with "he shall not become impure" — [since] he is [already] standing in his profaned state, we would not have had to apply "to profane himself" to exclude one who is standing in a profaned state, but rather for another derivation, as [brought] nearby.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:2:1.hebrew: אלא אמר ר"א צירף ידו לבית - כלומר, שהכניסה לבית קודם לגוף; משום טומאה איכא, משום ביאה ליכא — דמחולל ועומד:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:2:1.english: Rather, Rabbi Elazar said: He joined his hand to the house - That is to say, that he brought it into the house prior to the body; [therefore,] there is [liability] on account of ritual impurity, [but] there is no [liability] on account of entry, for he is already profaned.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:2:2.hebrew: צירף גופו - כלומר, היו ידיו צרופות ושטופו' לגופו ולא הכניסן תחילה — טומאה וביאה בהדי הדדי קאתיין. ואומר הר"ם: אף ע"ג דבית המנוגע אמר בפר' השוחט (חולין דף לג:) "ידיו טמאות דרבנן", אף כי מצורע מטמא באהל, מ"מ אינו כ"כ כמו מילי טומאה; שכמו כן בבית המנוגע, הנכנס שם טמא אפילו לא נגע, ואפ"ה נשנית במשניות דאם יש מחיצה כל שהוא למצורע לא יטמאנו, ואילו בטומאת מת — אף פותח טפח מביא הטומאה:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:2:2.english: "He joined his body" - That is to say, his hands were joined and pressed [flat] against his body and he did not insert them first; [consequently,] impurity and entering occur simultaneously. And Rabbeinu Meir says: Even though regarding a house afflicted [with tzara'at], [the Gemara] states in the chapter [entitled] HaShochet (Chullin 33b) [that] his hands are impure [only] rabbinically — [and] even though a metzora conveys impurity in a tent, nevertheless, it is not as [stringent] as matters of [corpse] impurity. For likewise, in a house afflicted [with tzara'at], one who enters there becomes impure even if he did not touch [the affliction]; and even so, it is taught in the Mishnayot that if there is any partition whatsoever for the metzora, he does not render [another] impure; whereas regarding corpse impurity, even an opening of a handbreadth brings the impurity.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:2:3.hebrew: הא א"א שלא עייל חוטמו ברישא ונחת ליה טומאה אלא אמר רבא הכניס ידו משום טומאה איכא - פירוש: משום דחוטמו עייל ברישא:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:2:3.english: "Behold, it is impossible that his nose would not enter first, and impurity would descend upon him! Rather, Rava said: If he brought in his hand, there is [liability] due to impurity" - Explanation: [This is] because his nose enters first.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:3:1.hebrew: הכניס גופו טומאה וביאה בהדי הדדי קאתיין - כלומר, שהיה כופה ראשו חוץ לבית, כמו "הלכוף כאגמון ראשו" (ישעיהו נ״ח:ה׳):
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:3:1.english: "If he entered with his body, impurity and entering occur simultaneously" - That is to say, [in a case] where he bent his head outside the house, as in: "To bow down his head like a reed" (Isaiah 58:5).

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:3:2.hebrew: והא לא אפשר דלא עייל אצבעא דכרעיה תחלה - ולא מצי לאוקמי [בבואו לבית אחורנית דלא שמיה] ביאה, כדאמר בפרק ב' דשבועות (דף יז:) ובפ"ק דחולין (דף י:); ולכולהו מצי למיפרך: הא לא אפשר דלא עייל מיעוטא ברישא, ומטמא ליה בטרם יכנס כדרכו:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:3:2.english: "Is it not impossible that his toes would not enter first" - And [the Gemara] could not establish [it as referring to entering the house backwards, because that is not considered] entry, as [the Gemara] says in chapter 2 of Shevuot (17b) and in the first chapter of Chullin (10b); and against all of them [the proposed explanations] one could object: "Is it not impossible that a minority [of his body] would not enter first, rendering him impure before he enters in the usual manner?"

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:4:1.hebrew: כגון שנכנס בשידה תיבה ומגדל ובא אחר ופרע עליו המעזיבה דטומאה וביאה בהדי הדדי קא אתיא - וצ"ל [דהוא] מסייע להסיר המעזיבה, דהא בהתרו בו למלקות איירי:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:4:1.english: "For example, where he entered in a chest, a box, or a cabinet, and another came and uncovered the covering over him, so that [contracting] impurity and entering come simultaneously" - And one must say [that he] assists in removing the covering, for we are dealing with [a case where] they warned him for lashes.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:4:2.hebrew: מר בר רב אשי אמר כגון דעייל [כשהוא גוסס] ונפק נשמתא אדיתיב התם דטומאה וביאה בהדי הדדי קאתיא:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:4:2.english: "Mar bar Rav Ashi said: For example, where one entered [when he was dying], and the soul departed while he was sitting there, so that impurity and entry come simultaneously":

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:4:3.hebrew: מהכא משמע, דכהן אסור [ליטמא לאחרים אף כשהוא מטומא כבר] לקרוביו, ואף כי מחולל ועומד הוא — דאף לפי דברי רבה, אם פירש אסור ליטמא, שהרי אחר שיפרוש ממתו ילקה על שאר מתים [אם] מאהיל עליהן. וכן שמעתי מאשלי רברבי לשון <abbr title="רבינו יצחק">ר"י</abbr>: שהנזיר יושב בבית, והוא עת כזאת מת בבית שהוא שם:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:4:3.english: From here it is implied that a priest is forbidden [to become impure from other corpses, even when he is already impure] on account of his relatives, even though he is in an already-profaned state. For even according to the words of Rabba, if he separated [from his relative's corpse], it is forbidden [for him] to become impure, as after he separates from his dead [relative], he will be lashed for other corpses [if] he overshadows them. And so I heard from great scholars [quoting] the formulation of the Ri: that the nazirite was sitting in the house, and he [the dying person] at that very time died in the house where he was [present].

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:5:1.english: "To profane himself" - It is written concerning an ordinary priest.

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:5:2.hebrew: עד שעה [שימות] - ולאפוקי מגוייד, דלהחלו משמע לאחר שנעשה חלל:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:5:2.english: "Until the time [that he dies]" - And [this comes] to exclude a mortally lacerated person, for "lehachalo" implies [only] after he has become a corpse [chalal].

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:6:1.hebrew: אמר רבי יוחנן משמעות [דורשין] איכא בינייהו - דהאי ממעט מגוייד וגוסס מלהחלו, והאי מבמותם:
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:6:1.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: The interpretation of the meaning [expounded] is between them - For this [Tanna] excludes a mutilated person and a dying person from "to profane himself," and this [Tanna excludes them] from "when they die."

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:7:1.hebrew: רבי אומר במותם - בנזיר כתיב: "לאביו ולאמו לא יטמא להם במותם":
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:7:1.english: Rabbi says: "When they die" - It is written regarding a nazirite: "For his father or for his mother, he shall not become impure for them when they die" (Numbers 6:7).

Tosafot on Nazir 43a:7:2.hebrew: במותם אין מטמא אבל מטמא בנגעם - אפילו באחריני אינו מוזהר כ"א בטומאת מת, שכתוב: "על כל נפשות מת לא יבא"?! [גליון: בת"כ] [כתב]: "במותם לא יטמא, אבל יושב הוא בהספד ובשורה":
Tosafot on Nazir 43a:7:2.english: "When they die he may not become impure; however, he may become impure from their leprosy" - Even regarding others, he is cautioned only against corpse impurity, as it is written: "He shall not come near any dead body" (Numbers 6:6) [so why would one think he is forbidden from contracting other forms of impurity from his relatives]?! [Margin note: In Torat Kohanim] [it is written]: "When they die he shall not become impure, but he may sit in the eulogy and in the row [of comforters]."
